svg.text: A · The two processes — forward is fixed, reverse is learned
forward q (fixed, no parameters): add a small amount of Gaussian noise at each of T = 1000 steps
reverse pθ (learned): one U-Net evaluation per step, T evaluations per generated image
The closed form x_t = √ᾱ_t · x₀ + √(1−ᾱ_t) · ε gives direct access to any t, so the chain is never simulated during training. Sampling must traverse it step by step.
B · The noise-prediction network εθ(x_t, t) — U-Net, 17.2M params, 64×64×3 in → 64×64×3 out
2.76M params (16%) — lowest resolution, where attention is cheapest
Encoder pushes them onto a stack; the decoder
pops LIFO and concatenates on the channel axis.
ResBlock(x, t_emb) — the only place the timestep enters
← t_emb, added as a per-channel bias
residual path: Identity, or 1×1 Conv when the channel count changes
1. conv2 and the output head are zero-initialised → each block starts as the identity.
2. GroupNorm, not BatchNorm — sampling runs at batch size 1, where batch
3. ≥2 channels per GN group. With 1, GroupNorm reduces to InstanceNorm and
removes the per-channel constant t_emb just added, cancelling the conditioning.
SelfAttention(x) — used at 16×16 and at the 8×8 bottleneck only (cost is O((HW)²))
D · Training (one step, parallel) vs. Sampling (T steps, sequential)
1. x₀ ← batch of real faces, scaled to [−1, 1]
3. ε ← N(0, I), same shape as x₀
4. x_t = √ᾱ_t · x₀ + √(1−ᾱ_t) · ε ← one multiply-add, no chain
5. L = ‖ ε − εθ(x_t, t) ‖² ← plain MSE, one term
7. EMA update of the weights (decay → 0.9999, warmed in)
Reference values: a network that always outputs 0 scores exactly 1.0;
a converged CelebA run settles at 0.02–0.03.
SAMPLING — one image, T sequential U-Net calls
d. x_{t−1} = μ + σ_t·z, z ~ N(0,I); at t = 0 return μ
DDIM: the objective constrains only the marginals q(x_t|x₀), so a reverse process
may skip timesteps. 50 steps instead of 1000 is a 20× reduction in cost.
η = 0 → deterministic (fixed seed ⇒ fixed output); η = 1 → ancestral DDPM.
